title: Ringed-site perfectness at the actual coefficient size
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site with object universe $c$ and morphism universe $v$, small relative to the chosen module sheaves [def-weil-size-convention], and let $R$ be a sheaf of rings with section rings in universe $r$, with sheaves of $R$-modules valued in that same universe [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Assume additive sheafification exists on the site and on each localized site, and that the maps it inverts are exactly the locally bijective maps. Use localized ringed sites and their exact restriction functors [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. A complex $K$ is locally strictly perfect at this coefficient size if, for every $V\in\mathcal C$, there is a covering sieve $S\in J(V)$ such that for every $f:U\to V$ in $S$ there is a complex $F$ on $\mathcal C/U$, integers $a,b$ such that $F^n=0$ whenever $n<a$ or $b<n$, degreewise splittings $F^n\to(R|_U)^{N_n}\to F^n$ with composite the identity, as in [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package], and a quasi-isomorphism $F\to K|_U$. An object $E$ of the unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] is perfect at coefficient size $r$ if there exist such a locally strictly perfect complex $K$ and an isomorphism $E\simeq Q(K)$. Bounds and ranks may depend on the covering member. No relation between $c,v,r$ and no uniform bound is imposed. The splittings are degreewise, not necessarily chain maps.
